verdicts.rewritten_summary: IDEHPUCP analysis by Miriam Tovar and Gonzalo Ugarte (15 Apr 2025) reports the Congress plenary on 2 April 2025 approved, exempt from second vote, the dictamen of the law 'fortaleciendo el derecho a la indemnidad sexual de los niños y adolescentes', whose article 5 bars anyone whose biological sex does not match the facility's intended sex from public sanitary facilities, with exceptions limited to accompanying/assisting minors, patients or people with specific needs. The authors argue the measure implicitly brands trans people as more prone to entering bathrooms to harass or sexually abuse minors, conditions basic rights on verifiable 'biological sex', and violates equality, non-discrimination and gender self-determination; they note Congress had already banned inclusive language and again rejected equal marriage. No Arequipa-specific finding appears; the source supports this record's critique claim.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Human Rights Watch (29 Oct 2025) reports a leaked draft of Türkiye's omnibus '11th Judicial Package' that would open the way to criminal charges against LGBT people — called one of the most alarming rollbacks of rights in decades: conduct deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' including its so-called 'promotion' would bring up to three years in prison, participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies up to four years (same-sex marriage is not legal, so such ceremonies are by definition symbolic), and gender-affirming care would be restricted (surgery age raised from 18 to 25, mandatory permanent infertility), with medical professionals fined or imprisoned up to seven years and transgender patients up to three years for care outside the new limits, forcing treatment into underground settings. It contains no Adana-specific provision; the source supports this record's claim that this national framework is what a visitor stands under in the province.

verdicts.rewritten_summary: Kaos GL's report on 2025 ('A Major Siege against LGBTI+ People in 2025: Hostility Turned into State Policy') documents six right-to-life violations, three recorded as hate-motivated killings with trans people the most affected (counted from media and civil-society reports because the state keeps no official hate-crime statistics), 89 torture or ill-treatment violations (up from 51), mostly linked to peaceful assembly, and 336 assembly and 313 liberty violations — a roughly 2.5-fold liberty increase mostly of detentions — with event-specific bans and violent police attacks on peaceful gatherings. It reports hostility institutionalised under 'Year of the Family' instructions to public institutions, hate speech from senior officials, censored broadcasts and cancelled artistic events, presented as national practice rather than provincial choice. No Afyonkarahisar-specific finding appears; the source supports this record's claims about the country-wide framework.
